newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco's BMCE bank merges A and B shares.
newsitem.headline: Morocco's BMCE bank merges A and B shares.

text.p: Morocco's Banque Marocaine du Commerce Exterieur, has merged its class A and B shares into one and increased its share capital to 1.44 billion dirhams ($165.8 million), a bourse official said on Monday.

BMCE had a share capital of 1.0 billion dirhams before a capital increase in April and May. The increase followed the issue of Global Depository Receipts on the international market worth $52.1 million, he said.
"Therefore the new capital was set at 1.44 billion dirhams divided in 14.4 million shares of 100 dirhams nominal value each," the bourse said.
The new line will be on quotation from October 14, 1996, it added.
BMCE announced last month results for the first half of year showing a pre-tax net profit of 259.3 million dirhams, up 17.7 percent over the first half of 1995.
Its audited consolidated balance sheet showed revenues up 6.1 percent to 1.2 billion dirhams in the period January-June 1996 compared with the same period of 1995.
One of the market's liquid stocks, BMCE was last traded at 407 dirhams on Monday.
